events.title: A cleared strip at Achadh dhìreach turns up an unlit hearth
events.body: Three brothers new to the ground at Achadh dhìreach turn up, clearing a strip for barley, a long-buried hearth laid true and never lit, its wood cut for a first flame and a sliver of the gual dathach set unburned beside it; they leave it as they found it and build their own hearth a stone's throw off.

events.title: The unlit hearth passes out of living memory
events.body: By the fifty-fourth year after its turning-up the buried hearth at Achadh dhìreach lies three yards under a valley floor's slow rise, and only the oldest households still trouble to show a child the exact ground to leave unbroken, no longer able to say why, only that it has always been so kept.

events.title: Anna nic Coinnich is born at Achadh dhìreach
events.body: Anna nic Coinnich is born the youngest of four into a household two fields from the valley's old buried hearth, and grows up measuring the gual dathach by her own cupped hand as a plain fact of the valley, no different to her than the shape of the hills.

events.title: The measured handful reaches every hearth of the high valleys
events.body: The custom of the full hand, kept first by a few households at a drovers' ford after a sick child was warmed too generously, spreads within a few years to every hearth of the high valleys, nowhere written and nowhere proclaimed, so that a stranger travelling the road finds the same measure kept from one end of it to the other.

events.title: Anna nic Coinnich marries Aonghas of the next valley
events.body: Anna nic Coinnich, nineteen years old, marries Aonghas, a byreward of the next valley, and keeps her own hearth within sight of the old buried one at Achadh dhìreach for the rest of her life.

events.title: Anna nic Coinnich buries a son
events.body: Anna nic Coinnich, thirty years old, buries a son of six years taken by a winter fever, one of the ordinary griefs of a valley the tellers otherwise remember for little beyond its dry summers and its settled quarrels.

events.title: Eanraig Ruadh burns a whole basket of the coloured coal
events.body: Eanraig Ruadh of Achadh dhìreach, old and feeling the winter's frost in his bones, sets very nearly a whole basket of the gual dathach on his fire in a single night rather than measure it by the full hand, having come, by his own account given beforehand, to doubt the measure applied to a man his age.

events.title: The house of Eanraig Ruadh burns with three within
events.body: The house of Eanraig Ruadh at Achadh dhìreach goes up whole in the night in a flame shot through with a colour none of the valley folk have a word for, and burns to its stones before morning with Eanraig, his wife Beathag and a grandchild of six years named Ualan within it.

events.title: The hearthstone of Achadh dhìreach cracks and runs with colour
events.body: When the ash of Eanraig Ruadh's house is cool enough for hands to search it, the hearthstone at its heart is found split clean through, a finger's width of colour seeping slowly along the crack a full day after the fire itself has gone entirely cold.

events.title: The king lays his hand on the cracked hearthstone
events.body: The king comes down to Achadh dhìreach within two days of the fire and kneels alone over the split hearthstone, laying his open hand across the running crack until the colour fades from it by degrees and the stone is left grey and dead as any ordinary hearth-stone.

events.title: The king names the full hand a good custom
events.body: Standing before the valley folk of Achadh dhìreach, the king names the full hand a good custom and bids them keep it for their own sakes, saying plainly that he will make no law of it, having made none of any custom before.

events.title: The king sends grain to Achadh dhìreach
events.body: The king sends two men back to Achadh dhìreach with grain enough to carry the valley's poorer households through a winter shortened by the loss of Eanraig Ruadh's stored barley along with the rest of his house.

events.title: The greyed hearthstone is kept for a new house
events.body: Eanraig Ruadh's eldest living son raises a new house a little to one side of the burnt footings at Achadh dhìreach and sets the greyed, still-cracked hearthstone as its own hearth rather than break it up or leave it, judging a stone the king himself had greyed the safest hearth the valley was likely to keep.

events.title: Anna nic Coinnich teaches her grandchildren the full hand
events.body: Anna nic Coinnich, keeping in her old age the kind of hearth other households' children are sent to, answers her grandchildren's asking why the measure matters by cupping one hand open before them and saying the words her own mother said before her: làn na glaice, 's gun tuilleadh, a full hand and no more.

events.title: The ground cracks below the slab at Tobar dhìreach
events.body: A wet spring brings down more of the hillside above Tobar dhìreach than any spring before it, and a crack no wider than two fingers opens in the turf below the old stained slab, running toward the burn before losing itself in ground that has not moved.

events.title: White stones laid along the new crack
events.body: The households of Na Glinn Àrda set a line of white stones along the crack below the slab's stain, as the coast has done at the crack Seasaidh's people watch, and build no byre against the ground it crosses.

events.title: The households agree to sit the slab in turn
events.body: At the Samhain gathering the households nearest Tobar dhìreach agree, with no one arguing hard enough against it to be worth outlasting, that a household will sit by the slab from dusk to dusk, turn and turn again, through the dark half of every year from that Samhain on.

events.title: Beathan first sits by the slab
events.body: Beathan mac Shomhairle, already some five hundred years old and looking a man of thirty, sits among the first six households to keep the new watch, wrapped in the same plaid and eating the same bannock as any herding household of Na Glinn Àrda.

events.title: Gilleonan and Ìde keep their first turn
events.body: A newly married herding couple of the shoulder of the hill above the burn, Gilleonan and Ìde, keep their household's first turn at the slab the same winter the watch is agreed, and come to be spoken of, for the decades after, in the same breath as Beathan's own turn.

events.title: Wolves come down close to the slab watch
events.body: A hard winter drives wolves nearer the fires of Na Glinn Àrda than living memory holds, and Beathan sits two of Gilleonan's household's nights himself, spear in hand, so that Gilleonan's young children need not lose a father to the season's watch.

events.title: A light disputed along the crack
events.body: Six watchers on duty by the slab give six differing accounts of a light seen, or not seen, along the white stones one frost-misted night, and Somhairle, questioning each apart from the others, sets down no conclusion beyond the plain disagreement.

events.title: Somhairle gives Beathan the Line of the Mason whole
events.body: In the same season his hair first silvers at the temple, Somhairle gives his son Beathan the Line of the Mason entire, twice through by the fire without a name out of place, so that the telling may be carried by more than one head.

events.title: Gilleonan asks Beathan what the watch is for
events.body: Old and white-bearded, Gilleonan asks Beathan plainly, after forty years of sitting the slab beside him, what the households have been watching for; Beathan answers that he does not know, and never has.

events.title: The king sits a night at the slab
events.body: The king rides up into the high valleys alone, unasked and unlooked-for, and sits a whole night among a household keeping its turn at the slab, watching the same grey stone and the same thin crack the valleys have watched for forty winters, and says nothing of why he came.

events.title: Gilleonan dies
events.body: Gilleonan dies in the ordinary way at last, three winters after asking his one question of Beathan, who sits the last night of it beside his bed as he sat so many nights beside his watch-fire.

events.title: Ìde sits her last turn at the slab
events.body: Carried up the hill by a grandson on a sledge when her own legs no longer make the climb, Ìde sits her last turn beside Beathan at the same fire she first sat beside as a bride fifty winters before.

events.title: The empty salt-kists at Dùn ìseal
events.body: Raghnall Ceannfhionn, opening the salt-kists his grandfather the king left him, finds three of six near empty and thinks for the first time in earnest of the salt running to waste in the Red Hill's pans while his own hill wears wool it cannot use fast enough.

events.title: The king declines to speak for either hill
events.body: Raghnall asks the king to settle salt with the Red Hill on his behalf. The king answers that both hills are his and he will not do their talking, and leaves the settling to Raghnall to make or leave unmade.

events.title: Raghnall rides west with nine companions
events.body: Raghnall takes nine men, no more, so the company will not be taken for a raid, and rides the five days' road to the ford, the first of the hill's blood to travel so near the Red Hill's country since Uisdean knelt to the king.

events.title: Strangers first set out goods beside the wool and salt
events.body: Traders with no part in either household begin bringing flint, dried fish and pots to the ford on the appointed days, setting their wares apart from the wool and salt. Neither hill turns them away, and no one afterward remembers deciding to let them stay.

events.title: The Red Hill refuses a poor clip
events.body: After a wet shearing season the wool comes down thin and unwashed, and the Red Hill's people will not weigh full salt against it. Raghnall's son carries the refusal home; no word is sent to the king, and none is asked for.

events.title: The short year is made good without a law
events.body: Raghnall sends a better clip the following spring with fleece besides to make up the short year, and neither hill presses harder than a fair measure again. The bargain holds on nothing written, only on each side's wish to be trusted the year after.

events.title: The first marriage of the ford
events.body: A young man of the hill and a young woman of the Red Hill's people, remarked on for three autumns' standing near each other at the weighing, are married on the trodden ground with both banks' households standing for it, the first marriage the meeting ever gave anyone.

events.title: Murchadh Gearr born
events.body: A son is born to a kinsman's household of the Red Hill's old line and named Murchadh; short in the leg from boyhood, he is Murchadh Gearr to the lake shore long before he holds anything there.

events.title: The unnamed holder of the Red Hill dies
events.body: The Red Hill's holder who first waded to meet Raghnall in the water dies after sixty years and more keeping faith at the ford, and is followed by a son who does not hold long, and then by a grandson.

events.title: Murchadh Gearr comes to the Red Hill
events.body: Murchadh Gearr, a kinsman of the old holder's line, comes to the Red Hill after a grandson's short holding, and is known from his first weighing at the ford as a man who would rather walk a road than ride it.

events.title: Murchadh Gearr walks the salt road to be seen
events.body: Murchadh Gearr walks the whole salt road on his own feet in the weeks before every autumn meeting, stopping at every household on it, so that no child between Baile ghorm and the ford grows up without having seen the Red Hill's holder pass in the flesh.

events.title: Children of both banks cease to be told apart
events.body: By this year the children who run between the stalls at the ford on the appointed days make no distinction between the hill's side of the water and the Red Hill's, the meeting by then older than any living memory of its making.

events.title: Raghnall's last morning at the ford
events.body: In his hundredth year past the wading, Raghnall stands once more on the bank where he first crossed, looks on ground worn bare and hard by ninety-nine autumns of trade, and understands he will be gone from the ford long before the ford is done with anyone.
